title: i95_route
description: Flat lookup against oracles/i95.json, Transurban's own published 95/395/495 Express Lanes network: resolves origin/destination (label or node id) to the od_pair_id(s) a future pricing tool looks up in trip_pricing_i95. No DB access, no traversal — Transurban already enumerates every valid direction+entry+exit trip directly, including cross-corridor trips billed as two whole separate tolls. Design: docs/oracle-tools-spec.md; version enforced by tests/test_tool_schemas.py.

origin.description: Ramp label (e.g. 'Route 267'), case-insensitive, or the oracle's raw node id (e.g. '182NO') as a fallback.

examples.destination: 495 Express Lanes End/George Wash. Mem. Pkwy.

origin.description: Echoes the caller's raw input string.

destination.description: Echoes the caller's raw input string.

legs.description: One entry for a within-corridor trip, two for a cross-corridor trip, in billed order (never chained or summed by this tool). Each is the exact od_pair_id lookup key into trip_pricing_i95. Some od_pair_ids (1374-1389) have never had a priced row in that table -- presence here means the trip is published, not that a price exists for it.

error.description: Unknown origin/destination identifier, no direct trip between a known pair, or (unreachable today) an ambiguous match.

valid_options.description: The full ramp label list on an unknown identifier, or the reachable destination labels from a known origin, so the caller can self-correct without another round trip.

examples.destination: 495 Express Lanes End/George Wash. Mem. Pkwy.

exit.label: 495 Express Lanes End/George Wash. Mem. Pkwy.

examples.error: unknown origin 'Route 276': no matching label or node id in the i95 oracle
